summary: PERCENT_RANK computes (rank-1)/(partition_size-1) for a row’s peer group.
documentation: PERCENT_RANK computes (rank-1)/(partition_size-1) for a row’s peer group. Tied values share a result, and a one-row partition returns zero. It differs from CUME_DIST, which counts through the end of a peer group.
inputs: scores(id INTEGER, score INTEGER NOT NULL), with distinct ids.
returns: id, score and position, ordered by score then id.
caution: Keep id out of the window ORDER BY so equal scores remain peers. The result measures relative rank within the observed sample, not a probability or a percentile interpolation formula.
scenarios: Show a score’s relative rank within a local sample.
Compare ordered bid positions while preserving ties.
Explain how tied observations differ under two distribution functions.
title: Measure relative competition rank
problem: Return id, score and PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY score) AS position. Present rows by score, id. Tied scores share position; a singleton gets zero.
hint: Use score for ranking and id only for final output ordering.
goal: Use PERCENT_RANK() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
